overview: Vanuatu brings together island communities with distinct languages, histories and customary institutions. Lapita pottery, food remains, chiefly places and sand drawings reveal settlement, skilled work and ways of remembering. The republic became independent in 1980; the peoples and cultural practices of its islands have much longer histories.

periods.title: The Anglo-French Condominium
periods.summary: Britain and France established joint colonial administration of the New Hebrides in 1906. Ni-Vanuatu movements later pressed for self-government and independence, which arrived in 1980.

periods.title: An independent republic
periods.summary: Vanuatu became independent on 30 July 1980. Cultural research, customary institutions and artistic practice continue within the republic, linking national life with the histories of particular islands and communities.

items.text: Quarrying at Teouma on Efate exposed a Lapita site in 2003. Archaeologists recovered decorated pottery and a cemetery, bringing evidence of skilled ceramic production together with burial practices. These finds concern early settlement of the islands, long before the modern state.

A 2014 study analyzed stable isotopes in bone collagen from Teouma and compared them with animal and plant samples. The results point to dietary protein from reef and other marine foods, wild land animals and domestic animals. This evidence does not describe every ingredient of a meal.

The researchers interpreted pig and chicken isotope values as consistent with animals feeding freely around the settlement. They also identified possible differences in access to protein. These are hypotheses about husbandry and food distribution, not direct observations of a household's daily routine.

Chief Roi Mata's Domain connects a residence on Efate, a place of death on Lelepa and a burial site on Artok. UNESCO dates the associated final chief to the early seventeenth century. Archaeology and oral traditions inform the interpretation of these connected places.

Customary tabu restrictions around Roi Mata's residence and burial place have shaped land use for centuries. Their continued observance makes the landscape part of living authority and memory, rather than only a collection of abandoned remains.

In central and northern Vanuatu, a drawer can trace a continuous line across an imagined grid in sand, ash or clay. The resulting design can carry a story, message or body of knowledge. Mastery involves both controlling the line and explaining its significance.

Sand drawings help people remember histories, kinship, songs, farming techniques and craft designs. A pattern can have several meanings in different settings. Presenting it merely as decoration leaves out the relationships between the drawing, its performer and its listeners.

Laplap combines grated root crops with coconut cream, wrapped in leaves and cooked with heated stones. Contemporary versions use ingredients such as taro, yam or cassava. The preparation brings gardening, grating, wrapping and control of heat into a meal shared at gatherings or sold in markets.

Simboro wraps grated plant foods in leaves and cooks them in coconut cream. The dish shows how leaves serve as cooking material as well as food. Recipes and ingredients vary, so a present-day description should not be projected unchanged into the Lapita period.

The joint British and French colonial system ended when Vanuatu gained independence on 30 July 1980. Political independence concerned the authority of the state; it did not create the island communities or the customary relationships that had sustained them.

The Vanuatu Cultural Centre's fieldworker network brings community researchers into documentation and teaching. Its 2018 film used interviews and archival material to explain how men and women record knowledge and support cultural renewal in their own communities.

ending.text: Colonial joint administration ended in 1980, and Vanuatu continues as an independent republic. Island communities maintain and adapt languages, chiefly relationships, food practices and art. The passing of an individual chief or a colonial regime is distinct from the continuation of the people.
